nextChange: Read-only final audit and recommendations; no implementation or project writes requested.

sources.summary: Owner-approved one-reader save/find/mark-read journey preserves title and address; excludes accounts, sharing and recommendations.
Local Node, JSON persistence, queue public operations and presentation/storage boundary; no open design decisions.
Queue includes read articles; mark-read preserves title and address.
Inventory and full rg/git file inspection show three documents only; no implementation, manifest or checks.
Clean Git revision 81feef422f8fda1c96302a7fb3c09070f60045ab; git 2.54.0 and Node v24.17.0 available.
This is an approved design awaiting implementation, not evidence of a runtime defect.

findings.problem: The approved journey has no runnable implementation. This is absent capability, not an observed runtime bug.
findings.principle: Implement the existing one-reader outcome in the approved local Node/JSON design.
findings.consequence: No reader can yet save, find or mark an article read through this repository.
findings.fix: When implementation is selected, build the smallest local journey with queue-owned save/list/mark-read operations, JSON persistence and presentation calling only those operations. Keep accounts, sharing and recommendations outside scope.
findings.verification: Exercise the actual local presentation: save an article, find it, mark it read, verify unchanged title/address and continued queue membership; reopen the application against disposable JSON storage and verify saved state. No custom architecture checker or delivery integration is needed.

findings.problem: The approved journey has no executable acceptance check or maintained product check command.
findings.principle: Protect the public save/list/mark-read contract using approved expectations.
findings.consequence: Later unit checks could pass while persistence, presentation wiring or preservation of article identity breaks.
findings.fix: Add one direct journey check using temporary JSON storage that covers save, list, mark-read and reload; verify read articles remain listed and titles/addresses survive. Expose it through one repo-owned native check command when code exists.
findings.verification: The check must run on real queue/storage and presentation wiring rather than mocked persistence, pass the agreed journey, and fail when marking-read loses title/address or the persisted read status fails to reload. Clean up only disposable test storage.

findings.problem: DESIGN.md does not state what execution evidence completes a change.
findings.principle: Proposed review principle: affected approved journeys pass on final inputs before a change is called complete.
findings.consequence: Contributors have no recorded rule distinguishing passing unit tests from verified reader outcomes.
findings.fix: If selected later, add one short evidence section to DESIGN.md pointing to the approved acceptance case and future journey-check command, requiring final-input affected-journey results. Keep design boundaries in DESIGN.md; use human review for presentation/storage separation until native enforcement is justified.
findings.verification: Review the section against VISION.md:5 and DESIGN.md:4-6; execute its referenced command once implemented. Proposed policy applies to relevant product changes; unavailable checks remain explicitly unverified and no exception permits claiming the journey passed.

limitations: No native application or native check command exists; product readiness is verification blocked. Audit helper successes are not product checks.
No changes were selected or applied; implementation recommendations are proposals only.
Goals, stack and terms are settled and retained; no vision board or interview required.
No declared pair of plans exists; overlap was not run. Measurements are advisory and limited to the declared revision range.
No external documentation or live dependencies were needed or researched.
Excluded router, akashic and no-mistakes commands were verified unavailable; no other skill or delivery service was invoked.
